region: Yunnan: Hani terraces, Dali, Shaxi, Lijiang and the Tibetan edge
title: China — The Ancient Roads of Yunnan
subtitle: Hani terraces, Bai courtyards, a Tea Horse Road caravan town and the Tibetan edge, by rail and hired driver
summary: A 14-day Yunnan route from flooded Hani rice terraces to Dali, Shaxi, Lijiang, Tiger Leaping Gorge and Shangri-La, using high-speed rail and a hired driver because foreign licences are not valid. March is the better month; the Lunar New Year holiday (5-13 Feb) makes February crowded.
introduction: Across thirteen days the route climbs from the Honghe Hani terraces at 600 m, through Jianshui's Confucian courtyards, to the Bai capital at Dali, the Tea Horse Road market square at Shaxi, Lijiang's Naxi old town and the Tibetan monastery at Shangri-La at 3,300 m. Trains cover the trunk legs; a hired driver handles mountain roads and each village stop. The days contain sunrise over flooded Hani terraces, a night in a restored caravan inn, a high-trail walk above the Jinsha River and Bai villages around Erhai lake. March gives blossom and dry skies after the Lunar New Year rush has passed.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman was self-drive, tents and empty desert. Yunnan is the opposite structure: rail and hired drivers instead of rented 4x4s, inns and homestays instead of tents, and densely inhabited mountain culture instead of emptiness; the independence comes from planning and walking, not driving.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Group tours rush Lijiang, Dali and Shangri-La in coaches. This route adds Hani terrace homestays, a caravan inn at Shaxi, a high-trail gorge walk and slow Bai villages, and keeps flexible days.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination offers terraced agricultural landscapes with several recognised minority cultures (Hani, Bai, Naxi, Tibetan) linked by a Tea Horse Road history and by high-speed rail up to 3,300 m.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound flight, day 14 return flight; one-stop connections; early departure on day 14.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: After the Spring Festival holiday (5-13 Feb) and chunyun return flows, with warmer days, Yuanyang terraces still flooded with blossom, and Lijiang/Shangri-La roads clearer; avoids Qingming holiday (3-5 April).

februarySuitability.summary: Cold nights, snow at altitude and, above all, the Lunar New Year (6 Feb) with a 9-day public holiday (5-13 Feb) and chunyun: high rail demand, premium prices and crowded tourist towns. Late February (after about 15 Feb) is workable but still in return-travel flows.

marchSuitability.summary: Dry, mild days (Lijiang 10-23 C average), terrace fog and blossom around Yuanyang, fewer travel-rush effects. Shangri-La remains cold with possible late snow; Qingming holiday begins 3 April.

climate.regionNote: Lijiang (~2,400 m) and Kunming (~1,900 m) figures from China Highlights averages, rounded; Shangri-La (~3,300 m) is colder and described qualitatively; Yuanyang (valley and terraces) is milder.

february.rainfall: Dry season: about 1-2 rainy days; fog on terraces.
february.notes: Winter nights often below 0 C at Lijiang; Shangri-La nights around minus 5 to minus 10 C (estimate, not source-verified).

march.notes: Shangri-La still near 0 C at night, days around 8-12 C (estimate, not source-verified).

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Shangri-La and Jade Dragon Snow Mountain can hold snow into March; the rail line avoids the highest road passes. Deeper Tibetan-edge areas such as Meili/Yubeng and northern Deqin are seasonally snowbound and excluded from this route. Tiger Leaping Gorge high trail is hikable in winter but landslides can close sections; check locally.
climate.airQuality: Generally good at altitude; Kunming and Yuanyang can be hazy; spring burning and pollen can reduce visibility (not verified for 2027).
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Not a wildlife trip; bird and spring flower season at Erhai and Napahai wetlands.

February travel means peak prices, sold-out trains (12306 releases tickets about 15 days ahead), closed small guesthouses and crowded old towns. March avoids all of this.

climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Fares to China typically peak around Lunar New Year outbound dates and for return from China in the holiday week; March is expected to be cheaper (not a quote). International fares to Kunming are one-stop only.

travelStyle.summary: Rail for long trunk legs, hired driver and minivan for mountain roads, walking in villages and gorge.

transport.summary: High-speed rail Kunming-Dali (about 2-2.5 h), Kunming-Lijiang (about 3-4 h) and Lijiang-Shangri-La (about 1 h 10, line opened Nov 2023). A hired driver covers mountain roads in the Hani area, Dali-Shaxi-Lijiang and the Tiger Leaping Gorge/Shangri-La road.

modes.description: Book on 12306 or Trip.com with passports; fares and timetables to be checked in the chosen app; sold out around holidays.
Booked through guesthouses or local operators; fuel, tolls and driver included; written itinerary and price recommended.
City transfers; Didi or Alipay-linked taxi apps; bike hire at Erhai.

transport.carRental: Not recommended: rental cars require a Chinese temporary driving permit for foreign licence holders and local rules differ; two drivers do not hold permits yet.

drivingRequirements.summary: Foreign licences and international driving permits are not valid in China. Foreign visitors with a valid foreign licence must obtain a Chinese temporary driving permit (rental cars only, small vehicle categories) at a vehicle administration office, and a secondary source mentions mutual-recognition agreements for some countries that could not be verified.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Not recognised in China (Vienna/Geneva IDP not valid). Temporary permit needed; availability and process in Yunnan not verified; some secondary sources mention exemptions for certain nationalities which should be checked with the relevant Chinese embassy.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four travellers hold car licences; each would need a temporary permit and the rental company must accept foreigners. Yunnan mountain roads, fog and dense truck traffic make independent driving a poor fit.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No travellers may ride scooters or motorcycles without a valid Chinese-recognised licence. Legal alternatives: passenger on a hired-driver vehicle, bicycles at Erhai, tuk-tuks/taxis and public transport.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Use high-speed rail and a hired driver with minivan; do not plan self-drive.

accommodation.summary: Guesthouses and courtyard inns in old towns, Hani homestays, mid-range hotels in Kunming.

camping.summary: No camping planned: wild camping is not clearly legal, village land is managed and cold nights at altitude make it unattractive; guesthouses are cheap.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Walking at altitude (up to 3,300 m), uneven steps in Yuanyang and Tiger Leaping Gorge; the long driving day (Yuanyang-Kunming) is tiring but not demanding.

itinerary.summary: Kunming - Jianshui - Yuanyang - Kunming - Dali - Shaxi - Lijiang - Tiger Leaping Gorge - Shangri-La - Kunming, using rail and hired drivers.

security.summary: The reviewed advice shows no 'against all travel' or 'all but essential' warning for the Yunnan interior route. Main concerns are arbitrary detention/exit-ban warnings, spillover near the Myanmar border (avoided), and road safety. France Diplomatie rates mainland China green apart from Xinjiang (read 27 Nov 2026).
security.assessedRoute: Kunming, Jianshui, Yuanyang, Dali, Shaxi, Lijiang, Tiger Leaping Gorge, Shangri-La by rail and road; excludes the Myanmar border strip (Ruili, Zhenkang, Tengchong frontier areas), Tibet, Xinjiang.
